label: Vanellus_tectus
summary: The black-headed lapwing or black-headed plover (Vanellus tectus) is a large lapwing, a group of largish waders in the family Charadriidae. It is a resident breeder across sub-Saharan Africa from Senegal to Ethiopia, although it has seasonal movements. It lays two or three eggs on a ground scrape.

appearance.colors: The black-headed lapwing or black-headed plover (Vanellus tectus) is a large lapwing, a group of largish waders in the family Charadriidae. They are medium-large waders with a black head other than a white forehead, lower face and bands across the rear head and nape.
appearance.wings: The black-headed lapwing or black-headed plover (Vanellus tectus) is a large lapwing, a group of largish waders in the family Charadriidae. There is a wispy black crest like northern lapwing and the bill and legs are red.
